subject: Decision Making
title: Algorithmic Fairness
description: A micro-lesson that makes Algorithmic Fairness usable.

hook.text: An algorithm can be equally accurate for all groups and still be unfair.

buildup.text: Equal accuracy, equal false positive rates, and equal selection rates are all valid fairness criteria.

discovery.text: Choosing which definition of fairness to use is a moral decision, not a technical one.

twist.text: ProPublica and Northpointe argued about COMPAS using different fairness definitions.

climax.text: Algorithmic fairness is not a problem to solve but a tension to manage. Society must choose which tradeoffs to accept.

punchline.text: 21 definitions of fair. Most contradict each other.

quiz.question: Why is algorithmic fairness difficult to achieve?
options: Multiple valid definitions of fairness exist and they often mathematically contradict each other
